marketMood: Cautious rebound as Asian markets recover from last week's Kimi K3 AI shock, but Big Tech earnings this week and ongoing Iran-US tensions keep sentiment fragile.

upcomingEvents.event: IBM Full Q2 2026 Earnings Report (after close)

topStories.headline: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 Wipes $3.3 Trillion From Global Chip Stocks in DeepSeek-Style Shock
topStories.summary: China's Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 on July 17 — a 2.8 trillion-parameter open-weight model outperforming leading US models on several benchmarks at roughly a fifth of the cost — triggering a global tech selloff that erased over $3.3T in semiconductor market value.
topStories.marketImpact: NVDA ↓ (briefly lost most-valuable-company status to Apple), AMD ↓, MU ↓, INTC ↓; global semiconductor index ↓ 6%+ last week; Moonshot AI valuation ↑ to $20–30B; markets attempting recovery today

topStories.headline: Chip Stocks Rebound Early as Peace Talk Hopes Emerge; SOX Climbs 2%
topStories.summary: US markets opened higher Monday on reports that US-Iran peace talks could resume, with the SOX climbing 2% as AI and semiconductor stocks led a relief rally after last week's Kimi K3-driven selloff; Micron and Western Digital each rose 4%+.
topStories.marketImpact: MU ↑ 4%+, WDC ↑ 4%+, SOX ↑ 2%; S&P 500 and Nasdaq cautiously higher; oil ↓ on ceasefire optimism; chip sector staging technical rebound from oversold levels

topStories.headline: Nikkei 225 Rebounds 2.2% After Marine Day Holiday as Chip and AI Stocks Lead Bargain Hunt
topStories.summary: Japan's benchmark rallied as markets reopened from the public holiday, with investors buying semiconductor and AI-related stocks at a discount following last week's 6.4% weekly plunge — the steepest in over a year.
topStories.marketImpact: Nikkei 225 ↑ 2.2% to ~64,946; Topix ↑ 1.3%; Kioxia ↑ 5.9%; Shiseido ↑ 5.8%; MSCI Asia Pacific ↑ 1.7%; KOSPI ↑ 2.5%+

topStories.headline: Chinese State Insurers — China Life, Ping An, PICC — Pledge Long-Term Capital to Stabilize A-Shares
topStories.summary: Five major Chinese state insurers including China Life, PICC, Ping An, China Pacific, and New China Life said they would deploy long-term patient capital into domestic equities after Beijing stepped up market stabilization efforts following last week's sharp selloff.
topStories.marketImpact: A-share markets ↑ on sentiment; 2628.HK ↑, 2318.HK ↑, 2328.HK ↑; rotation back into HK and mainland shares on stimulus and stabilization hopes; state support seen as a floor for near-term downside

topStories.headline: US Launches New Airstrikes on Iran; Oil Volatile as Ceasefire Remains Out of Reach
topStories.summary: The US conducted a fresh round of airstrikes against Iran and reported another American service member killed, keeping the Strait of Hormuz risk premium elevated and oil markets in flux as mediators attempt to broker a renewed ceasefire.
topStories.marketImpact: WTI and Brent crude watch (volatile, swinging on ceasefire headlines); XOM ↑, CVX ↑; defense stocks ↑; geopolitical risk premium remains elevated; airlines and shipping watch ↓

topStories.headline: Alphabet and Tesla Headline Big Tech Earnings Week; AI Capex Narrative Faces First Real Test
topStories.summary: Alphabet (expecting ~$101B revenue and $180–190B 2026 AI capex guidance) and Tesla (a record 480K vehicle deliveries in Q2) both report after Wednesday's bell, marking the week's defining moment for the AI spending narrative.
topStories.marketImpact: GOOGL watch ↑ on Google Cloud strength; TSLA watch ↑ on record deliveries and robotaxi update; IBM watch (full Q2 after 25% one-day crash); AI capex narrative at its first real reckoning of the cycle

topStories.headline: IBM Faces Full Q2 Reckoning After Historic 25% One-Day Crash — Its Worst Since 1968
topStories.summary: IBM fell 25% on July 14 after a Q2 warning missed revenue expectations by $660M; CEO Arvind Krishna cited clients rapidly redirecting spending toward AI infrastructure hardware, with the full earnings report due Wednesday.
topStories.marketImpact: IBM ↓ 28% YTD; consulting and legacy IT sector ↓ watch; AI infrastructure suppliers (NVDA) potential beneficiaries ↑; Wednesday full report is a key reset for the stock

topStories.headline: General Motors Reports Q2 2026: Pricing Discipline Holds Despite 4.2% US Vehicle Sales Decline
topStories.summary: GM reports Q2 earnings pre-market today with analysts expecting $3.13 EPS on $46–47B revenue; US vehicle sales fell 4.2% YoY but average transaction prices topped $52,400 as the automaker maintained discipline on discounting.
topStories.marketImpact: GM watch ↑; four consecutive quarterly beats with ~20% average upside surprise; strong pricing power thesis; F watch as sector read-across; US auto sector ↑ on beat scenario
